Dated this the 04th day of December, 2025 This Crl.M.C is filed by the petitioner seeking to quash Crime No.788 of 2020 of Mattancherry Police Station, Ernakulam, registered under Section 102 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Cr.P.C).

2. A search of the house of the petitioner was carried out by the Mattancherry Police, purportedly based on information that he had been constantly viewing child porn videos and downloading the same through his mobile phone.
In the search, two mobile phones were seized, and Crime No.788 of 2020 of Mattancherry Police Station was registered against him under Section 102 of the Cr.P.C.

This Crl.M.C. is filed by the petitioner inter alia, contending that the crime registered under Section 102 of the Cr.P.C. is not in accordance with the scheme of the law and the same is an abusive process.

3. Heard Sri.Prasanth K.P., Advocate for the petitioner and Smt.Maya M. N., the learned Public Prosecutor.
4. The learned counsel for the petitioner, based on Section 154 2025:KER:94747 and Section 2 (c) of the Cr.P.C. contended that an FIR can be registered only on receipt of information of a cognizable offence and that Section 102 Cr.P.C. is not a cognizable offence.

Section 102 pertains to the power of a police officer to seize certain property and it empowers the police officer to seize any property which may be alleged or suspected to have been stolen or which creates suspicion of the commission of any offence.

The procedure followed by the Sub Inspector of Police in registering an FIR,
classifying Section 102 of the Cr.P.C. as an offence, is against the law insofar as Section 102 of Cr.P.C. is not defined as an offence under Section 40 of the IPC.
Section 102 of Cr.P.C., thus not being an offence by itself, the registration of the FIR under the same is an abuse of process of law and non est in the eye of law.

Reliance is placed on the dictum laid down by this Court in Akhil C. v.
State of Kerala [2021 KHC 5051] wherein this Court had held that the registration of a crime under Section 102 of Cr.P.C. is not in accordance with the scheme of the Cr.P.C., and that such registration of a crime under Section 102 of the Cr.P.C. is liable to be quashed.

sentences.text: Thus, it is contended that no crime could have been registered invoking Section 102 of the Cr.P.C. pursuant to the seizure of mobile phones and charges on the allegation that the petitioner was downloading and watching child porn videos on the internet using his mobile phone.
The learned counsel for the petitioner thus prayed that Annexure 1 FIR and all further proceedings pursuant thereto may be quashed.
5. The learned Public Prosecutor opposed the contentions put forth and submitted that the crime had been validly laid after a due seizure that had been effected.

sentences.text: Terming the steps taken and crime registered as valid, it is prayed that the Crl.M.C. may be dismissed.
6. I have heard both sides in detail.
Police powers of seizure under Section 102 Cr.P.C. is ancillary to the investigation of a cognizable offence.
It does not by itself, constitute the basis for prosecuting an individual.
Linking the same with an underlying offence as defined under the Indian Penal Code or other substantive laws is necessary.
In the absence of such linkage, no criminal liability can be fastened, and no FIR can be sustained under the said 2025:KER:94747 provision in isolation.
Procedural provisions cannot be construed to create substantive rights or liabilities unless explicitly provided.
Hence, any registration of a crime based solely on Section 102 Cr.P.C. has to be termed as a legal misapplication of the statute and is liable to be quashed.
It follows that the FIR registered in Crime No.788 of 2020 of Mattancherry Police Station is fit to be quashed and it is ordered so.
Crl.M.C is allowed.

Sd/-
